subject: alt-f
title: ALT.F.------MT.INFO.
description: Diagram in The New York Movement section (NYM-3), opening the post-Ayler argument: 'a whole new community of musicians would solidify as a response to post-Ayler creativity, and the collective impact of this development would accelerate the vibrational voltage and spirit reshaping composite black creativity.' (C)ALT-F (alternative functionalism) is crossed with MT-INFO (music information). The diagram poses what alternative-functionalism's crossing with music-information looks like at the moment the post-Ayler New York School consolidates. ALT-F → PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance), with (C)ROTP (concept of responsibility-of-the-position) → PROJ-CONT *dashed* and PROJ-CONT → EXT-FT (extended functionalism) *dashed* — both conditional. ALT-F → SI (source initiation) → C-INFO (composite information) → (C)LK-IMP (concept of linkage implications) → EXP-DYM (expansion dynamics) → MT-INFO (the crossing). LK-IMP also → (R)POST (real postulation) and LK-IMP → STF (source transfer). Structural argument: alternative functionalism reaches music information only through the source-initiation → composite-information → linkage-implications → expansion-dynamics chain, with linkage implications as a hub branching into real postulation and source transfer. The dashed edges from rotation-point and projectional-continuance to extended functionalism mark the structural fragility of the post-Ayler position: their access to extended functionalism via projectional continuance is *conditional*, not guaranteed — exactly the precarity Braxton names in the surrounding prose about the New York School's economic and political position.
